extracted.intended_audience: PR / communications professionals at acquiring or target companies (startups and corporates)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical template and checklist for drafting and distributing a press release announcing a completed, strategic acquisition, including structure, wording, stakeholder communications, and distribution timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only for completed acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this template when the acquisition is completed (not merely a signed letter of intent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this template for LOI announcements or speculation; the release should reflect a closed or effectively closed transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic (not purely financial) acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the acquisition is strategic rather than only a financial investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize capabilities, market position, and strategic rationale rather than treating the deal as a passive financial transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material to stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the acquisition is material to either company's stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the deal will affect investors, customers, or employees materially, it warrants a coordinated press release and additional communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant customer impact required
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when customer impact is significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If customers will experience changes (service, support, product roadmap), address those explicitly in the release and related customer communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague buzzwords like 'We're combining forces'
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't rely on hollow or generic phrasing that obscures the real rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: 'We're combining forces' — instead state specific strategic outcomes and capability gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose financial terms when material
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not leave financial terms undisclosed if they are material to stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deal value or structure materially affects stakeholders, include transaction value/structure or explain why it's undisclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear employee transition information
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid leaving employee transitions ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State leadership changes, workforce continuity, office locations, and cultural integration approach to prevent rumor and internal confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address customer impact explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't ignore customer-facing effects of the acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what changes for customers, what remains the same, timeline of changes, and support/transition plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid duplicative/long boilerplates from both companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Long, duplicated boilerplates from each company reduce clarity and lengthen the release unnecessarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise boilerplates; for a combined entity, include a single combined description when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: state acquirer, target, and strategic outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline format: '[Acquirer] Acquires [Target] to [Specific Strategic Outcome]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the headline specific about the strategic outcome rather than generic deal language; keep it concise and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: one-sentence transaction summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Lede template: '[Acquirer], [brief description], today announced it has acquired [Target], [brief description], in a [type of] transaction valued at [amount, if disclosed]. The acquisition will [specific strategic outcome].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include acquirer and target brief descriptions, transaction type/value (if disclosed), and the acquisition's immediate strategic outcome in the opening paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 1 — Strategic Rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why this acquisition specifically — what capability is gained and what market position is achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about capability gains (technology, talent, market access) and the strategic fit; avoid vague corporate-speak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 2 — Customer Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe what changes for customers, what stays the same, timeline of any changes, and the support transition plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete assurances (service continuity, account teams, support channels) and timelines to reduce customer uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 3 — Employee Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail leadership team transitions, workforce continuity, office locations, and cultural integration approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about leadership roles, retention expectations, and how the companies will integrate culturally and operationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 4 — Financial Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include transaction structure, deal value if material, expected close date, and regulatory approvals needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide as much detail as is appropriate and material; coordinate with legal and investor-relations for public companies on disclosure timing and wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 5 — CEO Quotes from both sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Include substantive quotes: acquirer CEO on strategic rationale and target CEO on what the acquirer brings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both quotes should be substantive (not just boilerplate praise). Use quotes to underscore the strategic rationale and customer/employee benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: concise company descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide brief descriptions of both companies, or a combined entity if forming one, including headquarters and scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include HQ locations and total customer base/scale; keep each company description short and relevant to the deal context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for both companies
rubrics_metrics.description: List communications contacts for both companies, investor relations if public, and crisis communications backup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide direct media contacts and secondary contacts to ensure journalists and stakeholders can reach the right people quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-day coordinated release across both companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute the announcement the same day across both companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate timing to avoid one side learning news secondarily; ensure alignment with regulatory filing schedules if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate release with regulatory filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Align the press release with any required regulatory filings and approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan timing with legal/compliance to avoid premature disclosure or conflicts with regulatory notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer email same day as public announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Send direct customer communications the same day as the public press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize notifying customers in parallel with public disclosure to reduce confusion and support churn mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify employees before public release
rubrics_metrics.description: Employee notification should occur before the public announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform employees in advance to prevent internal rumor, manage questions, and equip managers to handle team concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use wire services plus direct outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine wire distribution with targeted direct outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wire services for broad distribution and add direct outreach to key media and stakeholders for earned coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — clarity of strategic rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should clearly communicate the strategic rationale for the acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the why is obvious: does the release explain capability gains and market position changes in concrete terms?

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — specific customer impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer impact must be addressed specifically, not glossed over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate if customers are told what changes, what stays the same, timelines, and support plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — employee impact addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should address employee impact (leadership, continuity, culture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for leadership transition details and statements about workforce continuity to reassure internal and external audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — financial terms appropriate to materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial disclosure should match materiality: include deal value/structure if material or explain nondisclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider investor and market expectations; consult legal/IR for public companies on what must be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — substantive CEO quotes from both sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Both companies' CEOs should provide substantive, not boilerplate, quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should add insight into rationale, vision, and benefits for customers/employees rather than generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — regulatory timing clear
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should state expected close date and any regulatory approvals needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity about timing and approvals reduces speculation and legal risk; include expected timelines where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — coordinated cross-company release
rubrics_metrics.description: The release and communications should be coordinated across both companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether timing, messaging, and contact information are aligned and whether customers/employees were notified appropriately.
